note: Structured, sourced knowledge base for the power-topology design agent (/design-power-topology). Captures the utility-to-chip distribution chain, equipment classes with real ratings + lead times, standard electrical pod blocks, redundancy templates, and Uptime tiers. The deterministic generator (drafts/sld/topology.js) reads this to SIZE a power chain and emit a valid single-line (drafts/sld/engine.js format). `catalogKey` maps a class to data/equipment-catalog.json so the cost model reuses the same pricing/products. Every numeric claim carries a `source`. Primary source for the chain + redundancy is SemiAnalysis 'Datacenter Anatomy Part 1: Electrical Systems'; verify exact ratings against the governing NVIDIA RA + project basis of design.

sources.tia942: ANSI/TIA-942 telecommunications infrastructure standard for data centers

voltage_levels.label: High voltage (transmission)
voltage_levels.purpose: Utility transmission into the on-site substation

voltage_levels.label: Medium voltage (site distribution)
voltage_levels.purpose: Campus distribution from the substation to unit-sub transformers; 13.8 kV common in US hyperscale

voltage_levels.label: Low voltage (data hall)
voltage_levels.purpose: UPS output and data-hall delivery; 415 V (line-line) / 240 V (line-neutral) common, 480 V in US

equipment.label: HV substation transformer
equipment.note: Custom-built to the specific transmission interconnect; MVA ≈ MW with a ~5-10% power-factor allowance.

equipment.label: MV switchgear / paralleling
equipment.note: Metal-clad, draw-out breakers, high interrupting rating. Contains breakers, metering, CTs/VTs, switches and MV cables. Paralleling switchgear ties utility ∥ on-site generation; ATS transfers to gensets on outage.

equipment.label: Unit-substation transformer (MV→LV)
equipment.note: One per electrical pod; pairs with the pod UPS. Microsoft pods cited at 3 MVA transformer + 3 MW genset.

equipment.label: Standby generator
equipment.note: Matched to transformer ratings. Diesel preferred (transportable, energy-dense). UPS bridges the ~60 s genset start. Meta 'H' building ~36 gensets; a Google building ~34 larger units.

equipment.label: Static UPS (double-conversion) + battery
equipment.note: Bridges the gap until gensets carry load. Eco/VFD standby mode >99% efficient but adds a few ms transfer time. Losses worsen at low load.

equipment.label: LV main switchboard
equipment.note: Group/fixed-mounted main + feeder breakers — the workhorse LV distribution board. In 2N, deployed as A/B boards.

equipment.label: Overhead busway
equipment.note: Solid copper bars, preferred for high-density. Tap-off units + whips drop to each rack. Replaces per-rack flexible cabling.

equipment.label: Remote power panel (RPP)
equipment.note: Transformer-less row/zone panel fed from a floor PDU or switchboard; branch circuits to a rack cluster via whips. In 2N, deployed as A/B pairs.

equipment.label: OCP power shelf (rack)
equipment.note: Central AC→DC for the whole rack, supplies DC via busbar (Google 48 V). Replaces per-server rectifiers; needs DC-busbar server design.

equipment.label: Battery backup unit (in-rack)
equipment.note: In-rack lithium backup; ride-through at the rack can eliminate dual central UPS systems.

equipment.label: BESS (battery energy storage system)
equipment.note: Ties in at the MV interconnection / point of common coupling (PCC), behind the meter. Buffers between grid-accepted power and internal load; provides fast frequency response, load smoothing, and reactive support — which accelerates grid interconnection (increasingly required by connection codes). A 4-8 h system can also serve the UPS ride-through role (bridge to genset start), i.e. a diesel/UPS alternative.

substation_topologies.label: Main-Tie-Main (secondary-selective / double-ended)
substation_topologies.tie: one tie breaker, normally-open (interlocked) or normally-closed for critical DC loads
substation_topologies.note: Two equal-kVA HV/MV transformers feed two MV buses (A/B) with two main breakers (N.C.) and a tie breaker. Loss of one source transfers load to the other bus; allows maintenance on one transformer with no outage. The Drybulb default MV arrangement.

substation_topologies.label: Ring Main Unit (RMU) loop
substation_topologies.note: Closed-loop MV feed; each RMU has two incoming feeders → redundant paths. Isolates a faulted section while maintaining service. Common where the local utility provides a looped MV feed; the RMU is the switching node between incoming utility feeders and outgoing transformer feeders.

substation_topologies.label: Distributed redundant (3-to-2 / 4-to-3, catcher)
substation_topologies.note: M blocks share a bus, any M−1 carry the load (each ~67-75% loaded). A 'catcher' variant keeps one reserve block online-unloaded that catches a failed block via Static Transfer Switch (STS). Applied at the UPS layer (see redundancy_templates). Beyond 4-to-make-3 = diminishing returns.

substation_topologies.label: System-plus-system (2N)
substation_topologies.note: Two fully independent A/B systems end-to-end. Highest availability (Tier IV), highest CapEx. Applied at the UPS + distribution layers (see redundancy_templates).

generator_voltage.label: Low-voltage gensets (≈480 V)
generator_voltage.note: 400/480 V gensets parallel on a generator paralleling switchboard at the site-distribution voltage and back up the LV boards; feeding the MV bus requires step-up. Common practice — the Drybulb default.

generator_voltage.label: Medium-voltage gensets (3.3-13.8 kV)
generator_voltage.note: Direct MV gensets feed the MV bus without step-up transformers; chosen on large (>10-20 MW) campuses to cut cable/transformer-yard cost.

pod_blocks_mw.note: Standardised pod size — widely available equipment, lower cost
Standardised pod size; common transformer/UPS granularity

redundancy_templates.label: Distributed redundant (4-to-make-3)
redundancy_templates.meaning: M blocks share a bus, any M−1 carry load; each UPS ~75% loaded

redundancy_templates.label: Distributed redundant (3-to-make-2)
redundancy_templates.meaning: 3 blocks per 2 needed share a bus

redundancy_templates.label: Catcher / N+2C (isolated parallel)
redundancy_templates.meaning: a reserve UPS 'catches' a failed block via Static Transfer Switch (STS) — ~2N availability, lower cost
